cases.purpose: Logger live CLOEXEC, exec noninheritance, one interrupted send retry, injected failure and short-send closure.
cases.oracle: The original deferral requirements, the documented builtins and independent Linux syscall/socket/fd semantics. Positive and negative controls use separate Python/ctypes callers in setup, never candidate output. The xattr writer changes a real attribute while its first data syscall is stopped; the kernel executes that read after the change and supplies the real ERANGE.
cases.comparison: A PID-bearing write marker immediately precedes the builtin. A pinned seccomp supervisor and VM-only wrapper record the marker, socket and other fd-producing calls, descriptor tables before each call, and live sender fdinfo. The unique same-PID Unix datagram creation after the marker must request SOCK_CLOEXEC; the send socket inode must be absent before creation and present at subsequent observed fd-producing calls and at sendto. Unrelated Unix stream sockets are allowed. Setup uses an independent sender with extra sockets on both sides of the marker and before and after creation; it also verifies rejection of missing CLOEXEC and a preexisting socket. Captured before/after descriptor tables, actual datagrams, return values and diagnostics retain the original strict EINTR, failure and short-send expectations.
